Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 26-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: CSE 1071/CSE_1071 PROBLEM SOLVING USING COMPUTERS  
  PROBLEM SOLVING USING COMPUTERS [CSE 1071]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               With a neat diagram of the computer organization, explain how each component coordinates             (3)  
  together to make the computer system work.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1B)               Analyze how expression evaluation changes if parentheses are added to the following line:            (3)  
  $$result = 10 + 2 * 5 / 2 - 3;$$  
  Discuss the above result before and after applying parentheses.  
  Explain the shortcut assignment operator in C expressions, with an appropriate example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1C)               Write a C program using a switch statement to check whether an entered alphabet is a vowel or a      (4)  
  consonant.  
  Analyze how using a switch simplifies the logic compared to multiple if-else conditions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2A)               Experiment with break and continue statements in terms of loop control and execution flow with an    (2)  
  example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)               A library stores sorted book IDs. The librarian wants to search for a particular book ID quickly.    (4)  
  Build a C program to search for a book ID using the appropriate searching technique. Also, justify  
  why the corresponding searching technique is chosen to be appropriate over others.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)               A teacher maintains the marks of students in two different tests as two matrices of size 3×3.        (4)  
  She wants to calculate the total marks for each student by adding the corresponding elements of  
  the two matrices.  
  i) Develop a C program to add two 3×3 matrices and display the resulting matrix.  
  ii) Explain clearly how each element of the matrices is accessed and summed using nested loops.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)               Develop a function named "difference" that takes two integers as input parameters and returns their (2)  
  absolute difference as an integer using C programming. Declare the function prototype and mention  
  the formal parameters  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)           A positive integer is entered through the keyboard. Write a C function to obtain the prime factors of    (4)  
  this number. For example, the prime factors of 24 are 2, 2, 2, and 3, and those of 35 are 5 and 7.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)           Implement binary search recursively on a sorted array. Your recursive function should return the         (4)  
  index of the key if found, otherwise -1.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)           A student writes a function void increment (int a, int b) to increase both variables by 10 and but       (3)  
  finds the original values unchanged when he prints them in main. Analyze the error and write the c  
  program by rewriting the function and print the updated value in main (Hint: use pointers).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)           Design a C program to analyze student performance using nested function calls.                           (4)  
  Your program should:  
  i) Accept marks of N students in M subjects and store them in a 2D array.  
  ii) Compute each student's average using the function studentAverage().  
  iii) Call the function subjectAverage() inside studentAverage() to compute the average marks for  
  each subject (demonstrating function nesting).  
  iv) Display both student-wise and subject-wise averages clearly.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)           Develop a C program that uses a structure to store the dimensions of a rectangle (length and width) (3)  
  and calculate and display its area and perimeter.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)           Write a C program to define a structure to store census data (city name, population, literacy level),    (3)  
  read data for 5 cities and display the city with the highest literacy level.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)           Develop a C program to copy one string to another using pointers only. (without using library            (4)  
  functions for strings)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)           Classify 4 cybercrimes where computers are used as a tool to commit crimes and explain 2                 (3)  
  examples of such crimes.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  
  -----End-----
